subject: Collapsing clades makes tiny compressed figure

messages.author: 389d046fc2d602cf
messages.subject: Collapsing clades makes tiny compressed figure
parts:
Hi again Guangchuang,

I am trying to make a simplified version of my tree with most subclades collapsed, just showing the general backbone of tree. But when I collapse the clade the and try to plot the figure, it is just time and compressed at the bottom. Here goes the example with attached tree file.

tree <- read.nexus("example.tre")
temp <- rotate(ggtree(tree) + geom_tiplab(), node=154)
temp1 <- viewClade(temp, 164)
temp1 %>% collapse(node=rimula) %>% collapse(node=169) %>% collapse(node=173) %>% collapse(node=181) %>% collapse(node=200) %>% collapse(node=208) %>% collapse(node=215) %>% collapse(node=222) %>% collapse(node=236) %>% collapse(node=246) %>% collapse(node=260)

I would like to get that backbone tree well spread vertically in the image to compare the backbone of different analyses. I guess one way would be to use scaleClade, but that is not possible after collapsing a clade (discussed in another topic). Can you help me get there some other way?

Thank you!
Tauana
